rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phase of acquittal and migration, prophetic speech aims to stir and prod its audience, while the people answer with stubborn obduracy; both appear in this exchange.
rows.anchor: His words are meant to stir the souls and prod the minds of his people and their reaction instead is of ultimate stubbornness and obduracy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question expresses amazement and distaste at the baseless idols Abraham’s people worshipped.
rows.anchor: amazement and distaste pointing to the baselessness of idols Abraham’s (sws) nation was worshipping.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols are Satan’s lures; Satan is mankind’s eternal enemy whose mission is to keep people from the straight path.
rows.anchor: They are lures of Satan and Satan is an eternal enemy of mankind. His real mission is to stop people from going to the straight path.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s declaration of acquittal is followed by migration, which he links with his departure to God and with the migration proclamation elsewhere.
rows.anchor: declaration of acquittal after which he migrated from his people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophet sincerely wishes his people well, but when they oppose his guidance and try to draw him into their ways, he regards them as his enemies; Abraham says they are his enemy, not the reverse.
rows.anchor: For this reason, Abraham (sws) did not say that he is their enemy; on the contrary, he said that they are his enemy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s creation and guidance of Abraham are undeniable realities and a logical necessity.
rows.anchor: The fact that God created him and guided him is an undeniable reality and also a logical necessity.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave human beings abilities, a noble nature, and intellect that distinguishes right from wrong and develops and uses those abilities; Islahi connects this with the Qur’anic account of creation and guidance.
rows.anchor: He has created them with a noble nature and blessed them with intellect which can distinguish right from wrong.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance necessarily follows from God’s act of creation: leaving people to wander would contradict His mercy and wisdom and make creation futile and unjust.
rows.anchor: The God Who has created human beings with all these provisions and with such wisdom cannot leave them to wander about.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since human intellect alone cannot secure their highest attainable status, God supplies their spiritual needs through prophets and messengers as well as their material needs.
rows.anchor: He in fact instituted a system of divine guidance by sending His prophets and messengers to mankind.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the source of all blessings deserves worship, not stone idols that cannot hear or see and can neither benefit nor harm.
rows.anchor: only that being is worthy of worship who is the fountainhead of all these blessings and favours

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating and drinking are God’s physical provisions; polytheists treated their deities as sources of sustenance even though they did not regard them as creators of the universe.
rows.anchor: they in fact regarded them to be a source of blessings and sustenance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham counters the superstition that illness comes from deities’ anger and healing depends on appeasing them: these matters are under the Lord of the universe’s control.
rows.anchor: A superstition that specially inflicted them was that disease was a result of their anger and remedy to disease depended on pleasing them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham attributes eating, drinking, and healing directly to God but illness to himself, both as respectful etiquette and because people’s negligence can contribute to hardship, though only by God’s permission.
rows.anchor: Eating, drinking and curing are directly ascribed to God but becoming sick is ascribed to his own self by Abraham (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection necessarily follows creation, sustenance, and guidance: recreating people is no harder than creating them, and this elaborate providence cannot end without consequence.
rows.anchor: If creating it the first time was no cause of bother to God, how can re-creating it be of any bother.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment is a certainty encountered after death; Abraham expresses hope for forgiveness rather than merely announcing its arrival, prompting everyone to prepare for that day.
rows.anchor: it is as if its arrival is self-obvious about which there is no doubt; however, everyone must prepare for this event

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham hopes that God will forgive those who lived in fear of Him.
rows.anchor: who spent their lives in fearing Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham presents the fundamentals of his preaching in logical order as personal impressions rather than argument, because in the acquittal and migration phase intellectual persuasion is useless; the subtle style may still stir hearts.
rows.anchor: instead of presenting them through arguments and reasoning, he has expressed them in the form of personal impressions.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham makes this prayer at the sensitive point of declaring acquittal and migrating.
rows.anchor: This is the prayer Abraham (sws) uttered at this sensitive time of his declaration of acquittal and migration.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥukm means decision-making power, a special prophetic blessing; Abraham asks for it because he is about to take a major step and needs divine grace and guidance for future decisions.
rows.anchor: refers to the power of decision-making, as has been discussed under verse 21. Prophets of God are specially blessed with this power.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having left his evil people for the truth, Abraham asks to live among the righteous in this world and the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: live in the company of the righteous both in this world and in the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lisān means fame or reputation; the construct lisān ṣidq means fond remembrance, more exactly everlasting fond remembrance.
rows.anchor: In fact, an accurate translation would be “everlasting fond remembrance.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks for broad, lasting acceptance of his message; the prayer was fulfilled through Israelite prophets and ultimately through Muhammad, whose message became global and enduring.
rows.anchor: Finally, Muḥammad, the last of prophet of God, made his message a global and abiding phenomenon.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the end of this prayer Abraham asks for a place in Paradise.
rows.anchor: At the end, Abraham (sws) has prayed for a place in Paradise

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham compassionately seeks his father’s forgiveness because a parent’s humiliation would be his own; divine justice rejects the prayer and forbids him to continue it.
rows.anchor: This prayer was not accepted and in fact he was emphatically stopped from praying for him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception about the sound-hearted is God’s own completion and explanation of Abraham’s prayer; if a child could benefit his parent, Azar would have benefited from having Abraham as a son.
rows.anchor: These words are not part of Abraham’s prayer. They are in fact from God Himself and complete and explain the prayer.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pure heart is wholly free of polytheism and hypocrisy; a heart afflicted by them has no weight before God.
rows.anchor: The expression “pure heart” refers to a heart that is completely devoid of any speck of polytheism and hypocrisy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Izlāf means bringing near; Paradise is brought to the pious as an honor, already adorned in return for their earlier good deeds, so they need not travel to it.
rows.anchor: means “to bring near.” Thus the first verse refers to the honour and respect

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is ready for the astray and only needs to be unveiled on Judgment Day, confronting those who had treated it as remote and become indifferent to it.
rows.anchor: The only thing needed on the Day of Judgement would be its unveiling. Something that people regarded far-fetched and had become indifferent to would be right before them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṣra means helping someone, while intiṣār means defending oneself.
rows.anchor: means “to help someone,” and

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intiṣār means defending oneself.
rows.anchor: means “to defend one’s self.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabb means throwing someone face-down.
rows.anchor: means “to throw someone face wards.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added letters in kabkaba intensify the word’s meaning.
rows.anchor: and thereby incorporated emphasis in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikhtiṣām means mutual altercation: followers blame the leaders of polytheism and disbelief for their fate, while the leaders say the followers merely followed their own path; the followers admit they erred by making them partners of God.
rows.anchor: means “mutual altercation.” At other instances

rows.speaker: Ibn Kathīr
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr explains that the followers treated the leaders’ commands as they should have obeyed the command of the Lord of the universe.
rows.anchor: While explaining the verses Ibn Kath īr writes:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels or jinn worshipped by idolaters were imaginary names with no real existence; the human founders who diverted people from God and rejected His messengers are the ones present to be addressed.
rows.anchor: the beings whether they were the angels or the jinn that the Idolaters worshipped were all imaginary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The followers first address what they say to their leaders, then the next lament is uttered as a yearning rebuke to themselves; context shows that they call their leaders wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: What is mentioned in these verses will be longingly uttered by them as a rebuke to their own selves.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The followers’ statement that they have no intercessor or close friend expresses sorrow and yearning.
rows.anchor: The words “So, now there is neither any intercessor for us nor any ardent friend,” express sorrow and yearning.
